column3: Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp v0.2.1-rc.2: exports ./src/* raw sources plus lib/index.js; ACP SDK 1.4.0 is a hard dependency, the ten @deepseek-ai/dsh-* packages are peerDeps, and dsh-token-meter is marked optional so the bridge runs without a meter.
Per-heading EN/ZH hash record for acp/README.md (41 section hashes); a doc-drift gate input, not runtime code.

Package contract: the ACP server exposes only the standard ACP v1 surface (no DSH cards, plans, terminals or elicitation), lists the calls (initialize/authenticate/session new|list|resume|close/prompt/cancel/setConfigOption) and the config fields provider/model/sessionListPageSize.
Chinese mirror of acp/README.md; same automation-only ACP contract and the same Known Limitations section, used for bilingual-pair hashing.
One pure function turnEndToStopReason mapping the harness TurnEndReason union onto ACP StopReason; 'cancelled' is reserved for explicit session/cancel while 'aborted' maps to end_turn.

Wire-content admission: strict canonical-base64 image decode, exact-route image-capability probe (llm.resolveModelInfo must declare image input), durable attachment store writes, and assistant-block projection back to ACP content.

Server entry: JSON-RPC stdio ACP plugin (apply/inject, AcpConfig schema with sessionListPageSize default 100), session new/list/resume/close, prompt, cancel, setConfigOption, authenticate no-op, absolute-cwd validation and additionalDirectories refusal.

Translates ACP MCP server declarations into DSH MCP client configs: stdio and streamable-http only, absolute command enforced, duplicate env/header names rejected case-insensitively, __proto__-safe null-prototype records, and slug+sha256 server-name normalization.

AcpModelControl projects the Agent's provider/model/reasoning_effort as ACP session config options; serializes mutations through a tail promise, pins one selection per admitted turn, and treats the empty opaque value as 'provider default'.

AcpSession owns one session's agent, prompt admission, update projection, cancellation and teardown; the InflightPrompt record tracks admission, turn end reason, and separates output errors from agent errors before settling the prompt promise.

Projects committed DSH session events to standard ACP updates: agent_thought_chunk for reasoning, agent_message_chunk for text/image, generic tool_call/tool_call_update, and a usage_update emitted only when both a token meter and a context window exist.

Machine permission policy: the two advertised one-shot choices map to allowed-once/rejected, unknown options and client errors fail closed ('unavailable'), and a foreign agent with the same session id is delegated rather than answered.

Main bridge spec (1005 lines, read in full): capability advertisement without private metadata, image-prompt advertising only with a capable route plus attachment store, session create/resume/list/close, prompt settlement, and workspace-path validation.
Table-driven test pinning each TurnEndReason member to its ACP StopReason.

Rich-content codec spec: image prompting is advertised only when every deployment prerequisite is explicit, malformed injected baselines and bad media types are rejected, and assistant images need a mounted store.
Connection-ownership spec: disposal cancels a running prompt, drains asynchronous assistant-image delivery before releasing sessions, drains continuable subagents before its own, and is idempotent.

Output-boundary spec: the exact committed update order (thought, usage, tool_call, tool_call_update, message, usage), foreign agents are ignored, output-conversion failure is contained outside a prompt, and a client that rejects notifications still settles the prompt.

In-memory transport fixture over the real agent factory and loop: a scripted MockAdapter, a real AgentLoop with testkit dependencies, JSONL session persistence, and a captured ACP client/permission surface.

ACP MCP declaration mapping spec: name normalization, stdio/HTTP field preservation, duplicate/malformed env and header rejection, __proto__-named env/header entries preserved as data, and provider schema failures mapped to an indexed declaration error.

Model control spec: absent route yields no options, an unlisted current route is synthesized into the option list, a temporarily unavailable provider catalog keeps the selected route, and an unadvertised reasoning effort is rejected.

Multi-session isolation spec: answers demultiplex by session id, cancelling one session does not affect another, each session enforces its own in-flight prompt, and bridge disposal drains every live session.

Prompt-lifecycle spec (990 lines, read in full): max-token stop, committed image delivery, cancellation, subagent delegation inside a prompt, and the failure paths that reject a prompt (pre-step error, inbox removal).

Update-projection spec: empty reasoning and unsupported blocks are omitted, usage needs both measured tokens and a context window, and malformed tool input is preserved as an opaque string rather than dropped.

tsconfig for the ACP package: rootDir src, outDir lib/types, and project references to cordis/schemastery plus session, agent, attachment, llm, token-meter, mcp-client, session-persistence and user-approval.

Account contract: authenticated Remote commands plus a snapshot stream that never returns tokens or PKCE secrets; getUnnotifiedBonuses returns null and ackBonusNotified false when the account is absent or changed, and watchExpiry is live-only with no replay.
Chinese mirror of the account-controller README; same 'no credential payloads' contract and same limitation about not resuming an attempt after the Host exits.

AccountController extends TypertRemoteService in the 'account' namespace: getState/getProfile/getBalance/getUnnotifiedBonuses/ackBonusNotified/startSignIn/cancelSignIn/signOut/hasRunningAccountTasks plus a watch stream and a replay-free watchExpiry stream.
Two-line type-only re-export of the account vocabulary; the module doc states Account Remote values contain no credential payloads.

Delegation spec: every Remote forwards to the provider unchanged, failures propagate as the same error object, watch receives the subscriber lifetime signal, and watchExpiry delivers only to current subscribers and stops on disconnect.
Sign-out impact spec: hasRunningAccountTasks reads running agents' latest logged request context, excluding idle agents and API-key (non-account) routes.

The Gateway contract in full: ctx.typertGateway.invoke resolves a generated InvocationDescriptor, validates exact named arguments, resolves lookup/Context identities and asks remoteAccess before dispatch; every call must name its Peer; gateway/* error codes name dispatch, binding, provider, lookup, context, argument, codec and uplink failures; uplink overflow is gateway/uplink-overflow.
Chinese mirror of the Gateway README; same resource-resolution precedence chain (resources reader > lookup provider > Context adapter > default field) and the same uplink-window caveat.

Resolves the resources one call or forwarded event touches, from Typert-validated arguments before any lookup resolves; per-kind precedence is resources reader > lookup provider > Context adapter > typert.resources default field, and an invalid resolution is refused rather than treated as global.

Client projection of generated descriptors: contributions install traced remote.<namespace> services with no JavaScript Proxy in the lookup path; it also normalizes worker-transport stream failures back into RemoteError/RemoteStreamCarrierError.

RemoteJournalStream layers cursor/page/live-tail coordination over a reconnecting Remote stream: opened/entry/notification frames, replace/prepend/append changes, continuity checks on every page, and a terminal status that closes the stream.

Client owner for forwarded Remote Events: registers per-listener Cordis handlers under a private UUID-prefixed event key, pumps generations, and resolves a Host waterfall with a result, a delegation, or a structured rejection.

Reconnecting single-consumer stream supervisor: annotates each item with a physical generation number, an accept() handshake for the opening baseline, and classifies a generation end as retryable (accepted) or terminal (not accepted).
Baseline-and-delta protocol over a reconnecting stream: exactly one opening snapshot per generation, deltas refused before it, and the previous snapshot staying published while the stream retries.

Client owner of the multiplexed WebSocket: one physical socket shared by logical streams, a revision counter for reconnect, an uplink pump with a bounded inbox, and RemoteStreamCarrierError for a physical failure a domain may retry.

Host dispatcher (1732 lines, read in full): strict vs SRC descriptor resolution, exact named-argument validation, lookup and Context identity resolution, cancellation injected into the last signal parameter, per-endpoint access control, JSON-safety assertions, and the Remote stream mux wiring.
Declares the 21 gateway/* failure codes in the shared RemoteErrorDetailsMap so the Host and Client faces see one vocabulary; every fault carries the endpoint and an optional field.

Wire messages for the Remote stream mux and the forwarded-event protocol: the /api/remote.mux route, $events and $events/result endpoints, ready/emit/waterfall/cancel frames, and strict parsers that reject any unexpected key.

Host WebSocket mux: one noServer ws server, per-socket logical streams bound to the Peer admitted at upgrade, Ping heartbeats with a two-missed-heartbeat terminate rule, and rejectRemoteStreamUpgrade writing a raw 401/403/409 response.

Carrier-independent contracts: InvokeRemoteRequest (namespace, method, args, uplink, uplinkWindow, peer, signal), TypertRemoteEventFrame/Invocation/Outcome, and the TypertGateway interface with invoke() and stream().

Non-page Client spec: one credential spans HTTP and WebSocket, a unary call completes while the lifecycle socket is still connecting, and interactions=none refuses $on and $stream while answer accepts them.
Test helper: provides an in-memory credential record owner and exchanges the Host's process token for a browser Cookie header via connection.authorizeIndex.

RemoteStream retry spec: generations are annotated and retry state resets after acceptance, one isolated retry is permitted while the Host is available, and a value arriving after disposal begins is dropped.
One echo stream exercised over both carriers, proving the in-process and WebSocket paths serve the same uplink semantics.
Access spec (940 lines, read in full): the resource-resolution precedence chain, per-kind readers, list filtering through allows(), and the invalid-resource cases that must not fall back to global.

Stream-host spec (1841 lines, read in full): uplink/iteration, abort-before-open, unary/stream mode separation, WebSocket multiplexing with per-stream cancellation, a broken error payload closing the socket with 1011, and the bounded uplink inbox.

Client spec (3477 lines, read in full): descriptor mount validation, arity checks, namespace withdrawal, worker-local failure normalization, WebSocket multiplexing without the RPC caller, and binary result decoding through a strict codec.

Host dispatch spec (1668 lines, read in full): strict and SRC validation, JSON-safety rejections (cyclic, sparse, symbol, accessor, non-enumerable), provider-mismatch and binding-invalid failures, and the exact business error preserved.

Journal spec (1118 lines, read in full): the opened frame, contiguous entry merging, repair pages replacing a superseded page, tail rereads when queued entries advance, and lifecycle guards before/after open.
Loader-mounted fixture service providing identity/hold/follow Remotes plus a pending() interaction producer, used by the authenticated-transport specs.

Connect-lifecycle spec through real Loader, HTTP and WebSocket composition: HTTP admitted before attachment, a refused second mux, slow stream cleanup delaying Operator release, and a fixture-path guard on temp cleanup.
Test helper creating an owner Peer per Context tree and an independent Peer per principal, so every in-process call names its Peer explicitly.

Event result protocol spec: delegation/result/rejection shapes accepted, every malformed variant rejected, and the removed logical-stream 'input' message refused; also pins the lossless-JSON requirement.
Wire-parser spec: every client and server message variant accepted, every extra-key or wrong-type variant rejected, and a non-lossless-JSON uplink item refused.

Mux server spec (734 lines, read in full): Ping control frames without application messages, the two-missed-heartbeat terminate rule, inbound frames counting as liveness, and a buffered downlink write counting as liveness.

Strict-vs-SRC spec: strict validation runs before the Service is invoked, SRC fallback tolerates an extra field, and a withdrawn strict definition fails with gateway/definition-unavailable rather than weakening validation.

Host face: six host-side source files compiled with tsconfig.base.json, referencing cmdline, host-webserver, remote-access, util/deque and util/timeout.

Job contract: job.list mirrors the session-visible set as whole-set frames, job.follow delivers one job's retained output from an absolute byte offset, and job.kill is a human's stop; both streams are non-consuming and never touch the model's job_output cursor.
Chinese mirror of the job-controller README; same 'cancelled by the user' reason and same limitation that the ring is a best-effort preview, not a transcript.
Client entry installing ctx.jobs; it resolves the remote namespace and job face at apply time because stream (re)opens run on caller stacks whose dynamic context has not declared remote.job.

React-free ClientJobsModel: per-session rosters replaced whole, per-job observed output with a bounded 128 KiB render tail, gapBefore marking eviction or resume gaps, and identity-stable snapshot caching.

Reference-counted client service: one roster stream per watched session and one follow stream per observed job however many viewers hold them, plus the kill passthrough and a resume from the model's cursor.

Host JobController in the 'job' namespace: the list and follow Remote streams plus the kill command, whose lookup and kill share one synchronous span so a producer-cancel throw is not masked as job-not-found.

Per-job observation generator: validates the resume offset, anchors with an 'opened' frame, coalesces output frames along a soft byte budget, marks a lossy resume, and closes with the terminal status once the job settled and the ring drained.
Per-session roster generator: subscribes before the first read so a commit cannot be missed, ignores output appends, and coalesces lifecycle bursts into whole-set frames.
Wire types for the job namespace: JobListRequest/Frame, JobFollowRequest/Frame (opened/output/status) and JobKillRequest/Value, plus the job/not-found error-details declaration.
OutputWaiter (a wake between waits is never lost) and an abortable sleep used to coalesce bursts into bounded frames.
Built-artifact smoke proving the generated job codecs accept a producer kind this program never compiled while still rejecting a status outside the lifecycle.
Client apply spec: the plugin declares inject ['remote','remote.job'], installs ctx.jobs, opens one roster and one observe stream, and leaves no state behind after release.
Host test harness: a registry with a 64-byte ring, a fake Agent registration, a push-producer job starter, and frame collectors.

Kill spec: an owned running job is cancelled with 'cancelled by the user', an already-finished job reports already-finished, a foreign session's job is job/not-found, and a producer cancel throw propagates unchanged.

Client model spec (578 lines, read in full): roster replacement and absence-as-empty, output accumulation and cursor advance, gap marking from lossy frames, snapshot identity stability, and reference-counted stream release.

Observation spec (305 lines, read in full): anchor plus coalesced output plus terminal status, a lossy evicted resume, oversized reads split along the frame budget, and the session-visible roster following a settlement.
Roster spec: the visible set opens the stream, another owner's lifecycle and output appends do not wake it, progress/stopping/registration commits do, and an aborted signal ends the generator.
Client face: four client files compiled with the client base config, referencing the gateway client face, client-store, core/session, jobs and typert-protocol.

Per-heading EN/ZH hash record for remote-access/README.md (8 section hashes).

Access-control contract: roles bind actions to resource kinds, a policy answers bindings() and explain() per non-owner principal kind, decide() is Gateway-only, list methods filter through allows(), and each Peer follows its own access snapshot.

Chinese mirror of the remote-access README; same limitation list, including that snapshot and list-filter decisions carry no call arguments and that an exact Connection Fetch route bypasses the Gateway.

Client face: reads the injected access snapshot, follows the Peer's snapshot stream, provides the remoteAccess service whose source(kind,id,action) answers for any declared kind, and publishes useRemoteAccess on the global resource.
Mounts the remoteAccess namespace and the global-resource Hook; a carrier loss keeps the last snapshot while the stream reconnects, and a terminal failure turns only a non-owner's answers false.

ClientAccessState holds the latest snapshot and caches one identity-stable boolean source per (kind,id,action); the closed/owner/granted union makes 'no baseline' answer false and keeps the owner's answers true after a failure.

Host RemoteAccessService: registerPolicy per principal kind, invalidate() to recompute open snapshots, decide() for the Gateway, allows() reading the invocation of the calling Context, snapshotFor() and the remoteAccess/follow stream with baseline/upsert/remove frames.
Eight-line constant: the globalThis property name __DSH_REMOTE_ACCESS__ carrying a page's opening access snapshot.
Access vocabulary: RemoteAccessAction (endpoint or event:<name>), Role, Condition, Binding, Policy, Decision, Request, the remote-access/denied details map, and the snapshot frame union.

Client access spec (291 lines, read in full): false without a baseline, true for the owner, injected-baseline validation with malformed variants refused, identity-stable sources per resource, and the terminal-failure behaviour that differs for owner and non-owner.

Host access spec (610 lines, read in full): per-kind role grants, the policy-failed denial path with warning de-duplication, allows() re-reading bindings on every check, and the first-snapshot computation.
Client face: five client files compiled with the client base config, referencing the gateway client face, ui-renderer, ui-slots and typert-protocol.

Chinese mirror of the remotes README (first 30 lines read); same build-boundary explanation that the allowlist files are listed in BOTH compiler faces on purpose.

Platform-neutral Client assembly: imports every selected /remote contribution as a runtime value, mounts them in order, unwinds the disposers in reverse on failure, and re-exports the whole client-safe type vocabulary.

Host BFF entry: registers the application event source with the Gateway, bridges synchronous Cordis listeners to an AsyncIterable through a RemoteEventQueue, requires a scoped waterfall to carry its routed Agent, and rejects non-JSON ordinary-event arguments.
The one forwarded-Host-event allowlist (28 entries) declaring emit vs waterfall mode and the resource readers per event; it is the single control point over what a consumer may receive.
Type-only projection of the allowlist into ApiRemoteForwardedEvent and the TypertRemoteEventSelection declaration merge.

Host event-source spec (first 150 of 296 lines read): the Host home is registered, each Client stream gets an independent allowlisted queue, and aborting one Client leaves the other running.

Per-heading EN/ZH hash record for session-controller/README.md (head read): per-heading EN/ZH content hashes.

The session contract in full: activation policy per endpoint (list reads only headers and cache rows and never opens a cold body), access control per Session resource, the Assistant-stream baseline with startedAfterSeq/nextIndex/compact stream, Turn-aligned history paging minima, the local submission echo lifecycle, and the archived-session gate.
Chinese mirror of the session-controller README (first 12 lines read); same summary and the same contract headings.

Agent activation and composition: ApiSessionAgentController owns create/resume/selection, the failure classes (NotFound, SubagentOwnership, CwdConflict, PresetConflict, StartedSinceObserved) map to stable session/* errors, and hasApiSessionSubagentOwner decides whether generic routing must yield the identity (first 150 of ~700 lines read).

Plugin gate on agent/pre-step: rejects a step proposed for an archived Session or a subagent descendant of one, following durable header lineage only (a fork is independent), with a visited set so a looping lineage terminates.

Host-side fold of dense Assistant frames into one shared immutable reconnect baseline per accepted revision; a revision gap or a non-dense chunk index drops the active attempt, and a revision-1 start after a prior attempt resets the accumulator.

Browser model catalog built from the live LLM registry: per-provider isolation (one failing provider becomes a failure entry, others still load), modelAvailable() for a GUI selection, and hasProviderApiKey() checking configured credential references independently of model availability.
Client-only event window: SessionEventLike = SessionEvent | AssistantLiveChunkEvent, where the live chunk is a transient row ordered between durable seqs by its own numeric seq (head read).
Outward Session face: components read lifecycle state through useSession and call behavior verbs; widening the interface is the explicit act of widening what features may do to a session (head read).
Outward ctx.sessions face: a SessionTarget is a Session id or a durable direct-parent subagent address, and an address owns no lifetime (head read).
Session-owned observable state excluding Conversation target data; a PendingSubmissionImage carries a browser-owned preview URL whose lifecycle belongs to the submitter (head read).
Client Session object layer: Agent scopes, Remote lifecycle wiring, and the re-export of the transport adapters (head read).

mergeOrderedBaseline merges an authoritative baseline without moving identities already visible to the client: baseline-only identities are inserted relative to the nearest following known identity and identities absent from the baseline are removed.

createScope mints a per-Client-generation Agent scope as a no-op plugin fiber whose context carries both a session-id tag and a Cordis dispatch filter, so untagged listeners stay global and tagged ones stay local.

Event-local acceptance for raw journal responses: rejects any unexpected envelope key and validates surface metadata, without stripping or normalizing wire fields; range membership stays a Host-side durable-log check.

Web presentation fold joining transient Assistant frames to one durable v2 settlement: it retains chunks until the owning step/end, rebaselines on revision or index gaps, and publishes exactly one settlement delta (head read).
Allocation-free narrowing of aligned wire records to Client event types, plus helpers reading a record's first logical sequence (head read).
flattenLineage turns summaries into a flat list with lineage depth: input order is authoritative, orphans degrade to root level, and cycles fail soft with a warning instead of hanging (head read).

Client catalog and durable projection cache: lazily resident Session instances, list lifecycle, host frame routing, and control baselines for uninstantiated sessions, using mergeOrderedBaseline so a refresh never reorders visible rows (head read).

Notifier batches structural updates in a microtask and stream updates by animation frame, rebuilds the snapshot before notifying, skips the rebuild entirely with zero listeners, and offers a synchronous notifyNow (head read).

Generic per-session projection store (push model): sequenced rows merge under higher-seq-wins, cached rows from a persisted checkpoint yield to every sequenced write, and no client-side domain folding exists (head read).
The Remote namespaces the Session cluster calls, narrowed to the commands, subagent and session faces it uses (head read).
Client catalog and source-labelled ownership of exact Session generations: it binds the Session scope, runs the manager and exposes retain/using/binding/retainInfo (head read).

The resident Client Session object: it stays resident after creation so its open Remote sources keep running off-screen, and it owns the local submission echo lifecycle plus the follow stream (head read).
Five-line browser time-zone sampler: resolvedClientTimeZone() throws when the runtime cannot provide a non-empty IANA zone.

Session-specific adapters over the Gateway stream primitives: the event journal (RemoteJournalStream) and the control stream (RemoteSnapshotStream), with the assistant-notification opt-in and its baseline (head read).

Session commands with an explicit activation policy per method: hasPromptContent rejects whitespace-only content, latestCompletedPrefixBoundary computes the default fork cut, and create refuses both workspaceId and cwd (first 150 of ~700 lines read).
Host-wide Session control stream: one complete baseline (projections per Session) followed by live replacement frames, with a per-generation queue that drains buffered frames before closing.
Thin Remote adapter over the composed file-reference provider; the Agent is resolved from the Session identity on the wire and the query and cancellation signal are forwarded unchanged.

Cold history pagination and the live follow source: page() reads without activating an Agent, follow() subscribes before its cold read, buffers events in a Deque, and carries the Assistant stream frames with a follower-local arrival ordinal (first 150 of ~430 lines read).

SessionController facade in the 'session' namespace: it registers the session resource kind, installs the model-selection projection, owns the agent/command/control/history/list controllers, publishes the api-session/* events, and performs background promotions with teardown waiting for admitted ones (first 300 of ~700 lines read).

Cold-safe list and search: the sessionListMetadata projection (blank means no turn has run), a work-slice deadline that yields only between complete rows, cancellation checked per row and after each yield, and a bounded provider-call budget for search (first 150 of ~400 lines read).

Authenticated GET/HEAD /api/file through ctx.fs: no directory containment, a CSP sandbox header plus nosniff and no-store on every response, Range ignored, and a byte cap taken from attachments.imageLimits.maxImageBytes.
Durable model-selection projection: 'model/selection' sets pending, 'request/header' moves it to lastUsed, and the wire view reports next = pending ?? lastUsed with stateVersion 2.
Type-only declaration of the five api-session/* events this controller offers to a Remote Event assembly.

Session-addressed skills/list that never activates a cold Agent: it reads the projected working directory and preset, prefers a live Agent's scoped registry, and falls back to the standing preset scope or the global registry.
Browser-safe request/result/lifecycle vocabulary for the session namespace, including the SessionListMetadata and imageLimits projection state declarations (head read).

Agent lookup spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): cwd-conflict descriptions, point-observation mapping to not-found, direct resume from a retained observation, lookup failure mapping, and writer-held detection kept distinct from other resume failures.

Gate spec (read via header plus 5 test titles): archived sessions and subagent descendants are rejected at any depth, forks are not, a looping lineage terminates, and disposing the plugin fiber lifts the rejection.

Client assistant-stream spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): durable window replacement, pass-through of durable events, chunk retirement at step/end, failed and interrupted retirement, and rebaseline on index mismatch.
Host accumulator spec (read via header plus 1 test title): stale lifecycles are replaced, frame gaps rejected, and each baseline cached.

Client apply spec (read via header plus 7 test titles): $events routing into the object layer, handleConnected once per generation, immediate control projections kept when the ready notification follows, a carrier-loss retry, and Agent scopes materialized before the list arrives.

Contract spec (read via header plus 6 test titles): branded Session positions at fixture boundaries, API wire numbers staying numeric, prompt parts identical to attachment intake, exact replace/prepend/append changes, and one settlement delta after transient rows retire.

Create and fork spec (read via header plus 8 test titles): default-cwd creation, missing Workspace and attachment failures, contradictory create targets, and fork failures for a missing source, a session with no completed turn, and lineage lookup failures.

Queue and attachment spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): queue edit/remove/steer, stale queue occurrences refused, one-shot and seed-only child descriptors kept behind the ownership fence, and attachment authorization read from known message content blocks only.

Upload spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): an HTTP route bound to the upload service, verbatim staging and ordering with an admitted image, bounded byte streaming, cancellation forwarded to storage, a prompt citing an unstaged file refused, and subagent uploads rejected before storing bytes.

Control Inbox projection spec (read via header plus 7 test titles): both pending lists in baselines and live frames, queue replacement derived from the completed projection, prompt rpcId read from a user-rpc source, and buffered frames flushed at disposal.
Facade spec (read via header plus 3 test titles): the Tools service is not required, Agent lifecycle projections are published, and teardown waits for an admitted background promotion.
Helper building tool-call, tool-result and user message scripts for assembled-client session tests (head read).
SessionFileReferences spec (read via header plus 1 test title): the resolved Agent, query and cancellation signal are delegated unchanged.

History-record projection spec (read via header plus 3 test titles): an ordinary event and its point cursor retained, one message with an embedded compact text stream, and an attempt stream with optional tool-name absence.

Inbox spec (read via header plus 4 test titles): the complete Agent-owned value stored without adding queue state to the snapshot, the highest-seq value retained before materialization, and no mutation before the Host publishes its committed value.

Lineage spec (read via header plus 5 test titles): root and sibling order kept while children expand DFS with depth, orphans degrade to root, a two-node cycle fails soft with every entry emitted, a self-reference counts as a cycle, and rows stay free of completion presentation state.

List scheduling spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): the work budget accumulates across both phases and resets after waiting, an override is honored, skipped-record classification counts, and cancellation is checked before the header query, after it, and during the last live row.

Manager spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): resident instances retained while unlisted, running retained for a row added during a pull whose baseline omits it, late acceptance applied to a re-added row, and a rejected first prompt staying blank across refresh and object replacement.

Media-reference spec (read via header plus 8 test titles): the inclusive image cap enforced for GET, HEAD and Range, a sparse 1 GiB file rejected before content I/O, post-stat growth rejected by the byte reader, Range ignored, symlink targets outside the cwd readable, and remote provider failures preserved.

Notifier spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): N markDirty calls collapse into one flush that rebuilds before notifying, zero-listener laziness, synchronous notifyNow, a frame publication superseded by a microtask, and a microtask fallback when animation frames are unavailable.

Projection discovery spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): V3 migration deferred without reading child bodies, a predecessor title hint served as a stale display fact only, a current-format cold catalog read from disk, read-prepared historical files reported as migration-required, and the live registry cut beating a conflicting cached hint.

Projection-store spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): a watermark only for current Host-sequenced values, higher-seq-wins merging, a stale baseline neither overwriting nor clearing a newer frame, cached rows filling empty keys only, and every sequenced write outranking a cached row.

Reference-ownership spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): an unknown identity observed without creating a scope, reference or history request, the shared initial opening with independent source contributions, repeated-use counting, a cancelled waiter not cancelling another's opening, and a same-id replacement withdrawing the old generation first.

Access spec (read via header plus 7 test titles): the controller owns the session resource kind with the sessionId default field, page and follow read the addressed Session, a global role may call session/list while a Session role decides the rows, non-owner search hits are filtered, control baselines and projection frames are filtered, and a non-owner caller is recorded on the prompt source.

Scope primitive spec (read via header plus 6 test titles): same-id generations route independently while untagged listeners stay shared, scopeOf tags the context, a subject-less root dispatch is unfiltered, and fiber disposal removes scope-owned listeners.

Cold-session spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): listed format status preserved, a predecessor title hint used with zero cold stat or body reads, cold rows served from cached projections, updatedAt tracking only human prompts, and the stored interrupted prefix served verbatim without activating the session.

Fork spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): required migration reported before forking when disallowed, a resident session forked without disk metadata, a stat failure not treated as migration, the completed manual compaction checkpoint kept when atSeq is omitted, an exact cut at a completed turn, and a subagent fork attached to its nearest workspace-owning ancestor.

History-journal spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): an empty opted-in Assistant baseline before any live attempt, foreign and opening-baseline frames filtered, mixed live FIFO order preserved, revision one forwarded when the Agent lifecycle restarts, an empty replacement baseline after a revision gap, and Assistant frames from another Session filtered out.
Blank-bit spec (read via header plus 2 test titles): standalone events (command lifecycle, plan/mode, title) keep the session blank, and the first turn clears blank.

Model spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): an ordered image batch validated before any member is persisted, an admitted image batch delivered through steer with the same ordering as queue, attachment bytes authorized only when the session event stream references the id, provider grouping with an unlisted current selection left out, and an unlisted model rejected.

Workspace-path spec (read via header plus 8 test titles): opener capability reported independently of a Session, availability derived from config, an injected opener or the platform probe, a Client-resolved path handed over unchanged, empty paths rejected before opening, and reveal dispatched separately from default-app open.

Submission-echo spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): the echo inserted synchronously before any prompt call, placement derived from running state and delivery mode, rapid submissions kept in Chat until the running update arrives, a rejected identified prompt retiring its echo immediately, and the echo identity sent as the prompt requestId.

Preset spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): the requested preset recorded on the Session header, the roster default used when none is named, an unknown preset rejected, a header left preset-less with no roster, and a blank Session recomposed under the default or the named preset.

Projection spec (read via header plus 9 test titles): the v0 numeric seed cut kept on the wire, pending and used model selections tracked across request headers, the tail page serving the unit value with asOfSeq = last event seq, a cold persisted queue reconstructed without publishing an Agent, claimed steering removed from the pending Inbox projection, and the imageLimits key absent while no attachment service is composed.
Rejection spec (read via header plus 2 test titles): a rejecting Remote face propagates from prompt, cancel, subagent continuation prompt and interrupt while recording no prompt error.

Rename spec (read via header plus 4 test titles): acceptance through the composed title service with a normalized user-source event and echoed seq, only an empty-normalizing title mapping to title-invalid, a non-validation failure mapping to internal, and internal when no title service is composed.

Search spec (read via header plus 10 test titles): search rejected when the query service is absent, only list-visible ids and conversation-message events searched, invalid wire queries rejected before the provider, an empty page without invoking the index, a violating provider snippet rejected, the globally ranked stream paged to the 20-item boundary, a learned provider limit of 10, and the page-limit probe counted inside the 100-call budget.

Skill-catalog spec (read via header plus 7 test titles): a moved cold Session catalog read from its recorded current directory without resuming an Agent, a live Agent addressing a preset-owned registry, the recorded preset standing scope for a cold Session, a fallback to the global registry, an absent registry reported instead of an empty catalog, and observations without projections rejected.
